validity.candidate_value: Confirmed genuine -- not a duplicate, not misclassified
validity.recommendation: No existence/duplicate/classification action needed. The row is a real, well-documented (2018-2025 coverage across independent Russian outlets) pipeline with an unusually complex but internally coherent history: originally the Eastern route of the Southern Corridor / South Stream feeder (design capacity 63 bcm/y); ~500 km built by ~2016 when Gazprom recognized a ~46bn RUB impairment for unfinished South-Stream-related construction; in 2017-2018 Gazprom planned to LIQUIDATE 506 km of specific built sections (km347.5-493, km493-661, km834-963.7, km1168.1-1231, plus the Mokshanskaya gas-measuring station) because Turkish Stream halved the required capacity to 31.5 bcm/y (interfax.ru/business/604208, 2018-03-19); Gazprom then reversed course in Dec 2018/2019 and resumed construction to serve the domestic market instead; May/July 2022 saw the new 1420mm section connected to the Urengoy-Pomary-Uzhgorod corridor and first gas supplied (rg.ru via Wayback); construction/design-approval activity continued in 2021 (neftegaz.ru/672905) and tendering/construction activity is still ongoing as of 2025 (t.me/gspromru contractor channel; see Status fill). Notably, the km347.5-493 segment slated for liquidation in 2017/2018 appears to be the SAME segment later subject to a July 2024 'commissioning under load' tender per gem.wiki's own footnote [13] -- i.e. apparently rebuilt/recommissioned after a near-liquidation, not evidence of a duplicate or erroneous row. StartYear1=2023 should be read as a phased/partial milestone (see Start fill's caveat), not full-system commissioning -- no source names a new full-line target year.
validity.researcher_notes: This context does not itself resolve the SegmentCost question (separate 'spec' concern filed) but confirms the pipeline's existence, single ownership (Gazprom PJSC, see Owner fill), and current construction status are all solid.
